response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), a AS (SELECT AVG(n * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.n * 1.0) AS avg_invoiced_orders, AVG(g.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.n > a.avg_n;

assumptions.assumption: Customers with a NULL gender form one group, which GROUP BY produces naturally. Empty-string genders, if any exist, stay a separate group and are not merged with NULL.
Only genders with at least one invoiced order appear in the per-gender counts, because the counts are built from invoices. Genders with no invoiced orders are not included in the overall average.
